You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The pattern: the fed funds rate is high relative to its 3-year average (+1.5) but falling fast (3m change -2.0), the 2-year yield is down sharply, and the unemployment rate is low relative to its history (-1.5) but dropping, which seems odd. Industrial production is falling sharply, and the national activity index is weak. Credit spreads are widening and Treasuries are rallying.

This looks like late 2007 to early 2008, or possibly 2019. Check the 2007 candidate. A 36-month window ending in late 2007 would cover 2005-2007, when rates were rising, so the policy rate would be high at +1.5. A 3m change of -2.0 fits the Fed cutting from September 2007. The 12m change of 0.0 fits too, since the rate was 5.25% in late 2006. The 2-year yield is down 2.5 over 3m and 10-year yields are lower. Unemployment at -1.5 z-score fits 4.7% against a higher 2004-05 level. Headline CPI is +1.0 over 3m, consistent with the oil spike. Equities are down 2% over 1m, and the 12m return is -1.5 z-score, which looks odd for 2007 but may reflect the standardization.

Alternatively, the December 2007 to January 2008 period fits: equities fell in November 2007 and January 2008. The 3m equity change is only -1.0, and the 3m Treasury gain is +2.0. The 12m change in the spread is 0.0, with a curve at -1.5, which seems inconsistent with 2007 because the curve was steepening by then. In 2019 the curve was inverted at -1.5 relative to its own history, which fits better. But the policy rate in 2019 was above its 3-year average, and the Fed was cutting by 3m -2.0 in October 2019. Yet IP was falling in 2019 and unemployment was low at -1.5, which fits as well. Headline CPI 12m change of -1.5 fits 2019, when inflation fell from 2.9% to 1.8%. VIX +0.5 and equity 12m return -1.5 are odd for 2019, though.

The best candidate is August 2019: the 10y yield plunged, equities fell 2% in the month, the Fed cut in July, and the 2y fell. Equity-bond correlation was negative. The policy rate 3m change of -2.0 may reflect the z-score of a small change. In August 2019 the Fed had cut only once. The 12m equity return was around 2%, though, versus a 3-year average around 10%, so -1.5 is plausible. The 3m return at -1.0 is plausible as well.

Choose August 2019, though the time window is uncertain.
